cards: Harald Fairhair is remembered as the first king of a united Norway.
Sviatoslav I of Kiev was a prince of Kievan Rus in the tenth century.
Henry the Fowler, Duke of Saxony, was elected king of East Francia in 919, the first of the Ottonian dynasty.
Æthelstan was king of the Anglo-Saxons from 924 and the first king of all England from 927, when he took York and received the submission of northern rulers.
Otto I, Duke of Saxony and King of Germany, was crowned emperor by Pope John XII in 962 CE.
Almanzor (al-Mansur, 'the Victorious'), born Muhammad ibn Abi Amir, was the hajib (chief minister) and real ruler of the Caliphate of Córdoba from 978, governing for the young caliph Hisham II.
Æthelflæd, Lady of the Mercians, was the eldest daughter of Alfred the Great and ruled English Mercia from the death of her husband Æthelred in 911 until her own death in 918.
Edward the Elder was King of the Anglo-Saxons from 899 to 924, son of Alfred the Great.
Harald Bluetooth was King of Denmark from about 958 to about 986, the son of Gorm the Old.
Hugh Capet was Duke of the Franks and, from 987, King of the Franks, the founder of the Capetian dynasty.
Hywel Dda, Hywel the Good, was a Welsh king, grandson of Rhodri the Great.
Constantine VII Porphyrogenitus was Byzantine emperor, nominally from 913 and in real power from 945 to 959.
Emperor Taizu, born Zhao Kuangyin, was the founder of the Song Dynasty.
John I Tzimiskes was Byzantine emperor from 969 to 976, an Armenian-born general who seized the throne by murdering his uncle Nikephoros II Phokas.
Oleg of Novgorod was a Varangian prince who, according to the Primary Chronicle, succeeded Rurik at Novgorod and in 882 seized Kiev, killing its rulers Askold and Dir.
Taejo of Goryeo, born Wang Geon, was the founder of the Goryeo dynasty of Korea.
Hugh of Arles, also called Hugh of Provence, was count of Arles and Vienne and effective ruler of Provence before becoming King of Italy in 926.
Olaf Tryggvason was king of Norway from 995 to 1000.
Pope Sylvester II, born Gerbert of Aurillac, was a French scholar who became the first French pope, reigning from 999 to 1003.
Sweyn Forkbeard (c. 960–1014) was King of Denmark from about 986, after rebelling against his father Harald Bluetooth, and from 1000 also overlord of Norway.
Æthelred was the ruler of English Mercia from about 881 until his death in 911, after the Danes had taken the eastern half of the kingdom.
Widukind of Corvey was a Saxon monk of the abbey of Corvey and author of the Deeds of the Saxons (Res gestae Saxonicae), written in the late 960s and early 970s.
Brian Boru was King of Munster from the Dál Cais dynasty and High King of Ireland from 1002.
Chavundaraya was a minister and military commander of the Western Ganga kings Marasimha II and Rachamalla IV in the late 10th century.
Gero the Great was a Saxon noble whom Otto I appointed in 937 to command the eastern frontier of Saxony against the Slavs.
Gung Ye was a warlord of Korea's Later Three Kingdoms period, said to be an outcast Silla prince who lost an eye as an infant and became a Buddhist monk.
Al-Masudi was an Arab historian and geographer from Baghdad, often called the Herodotus of the Arabs.
Adud al-Dawla was the greatest ruler of the Buyid dynasty.
Borrell II was Count of Barcelona, Girona and Osona from 947 and Count of Urgell from 948.
Mardavij ibn Ziyar was a Gilite military leader who founded the Ziyarid dynasty in northern Iran.
Ordoño II was a son of Alfonso III of Asturias who received Galicia when his father's realm was divided in 910.
Rollo was a Viking leader of Scandinavian origin who founded the Norman principality on the lower Seine.
Sancho I, called the Fat, was King of León from 956 to 958 and again from 960 to 966.
Toda of Pamplona was queen consort of Sancho I Garcés of Pamplona and regent for their son García Sánchez I.
William the Pious was count of Auvergne and, from 893, duke of Aquitaine, one of the greatest nobles of the late Carolingian kingdom.
William Longsword was the son of Rollo and ruler of Normandy from about 927 to 942.
Alan II, called Barbetorte or Twisted Beard, was a grandson of Alan the Great who grew up in exile in England.
Bagrat III of the Bagrationi dynasty was the first king of a united Georgia.
Eric the Victorious was a king of the Swedes around Uppsala in the late 10th century, the first Swedish king known with reasonable certainty.
Li Cunxu was the son of the Shatuo Turk warlord Li Keyong and his successor as Prince of Jin from 908.
